prompt: Classify three side lengths as equilateral, isosceles or scalene -- but only after rejecting the lengths that cannot form a triangle at all. Complete classify in TriangleClassifier.
explanation: Guard clauses put the impossible cases first: once the non-positive sides and the triangle-inequality failures have returned "invalid", the rest of the method can assume it really has a triangle. Checking all three inequalities (a+b>c, a+c>b, b+c>a) avoids having to sort the sides to find the longest. The shape tests then run from most specific to least: all three equal, then any two equal, and scalene as the fall-through answer.
hints: Handle the two rejection rules with early returns before you compare sides for equality.
The triangle inequality must hold for every pairing: a + b > c, a + c > b and b + c > a. Using <= catches the degenerate 1, 2, 3 case.
Test equilateral (a == b && b == c) before isosceles, otherwise every equilateral triangle answers "isosceles".
